logs: New: An AI assistant connected through MCP (p202 mcp, or Tracking202's hosted MCP server) renames and deletes traffic sources, their accounts and categories: ppc_network_update, ppc_account_update and aff_network_update run p202 ppc-network, ppc-account and aff-network update (a rename, an account's default flag, an account moved to another of your sources), and ppc_network_delete, ppc_account_delete and aff_network_delete their delete (dry_run first). Until now it could only list and create them, so asked to rename "Google Ads - Main" to "Main" it could only make a second source. A delete removes that one record, as Setup › Traffic Sources and Setup › Categories do: a traffic source's accounts and a category's campaigns stay, and each tool's description says so. A hosted connection needs no new approval for them: the access it was approved with already covers traffic sources and categories

Changed: A visitor who comes back through a redirector link (a re-click) is counted once in every report, under the visit they made last, with the traffic source and cost of their first visit, and a conversion is credited to that last visit. Update CPC chooses such a click by its first visit and sets the cost of every visit

Changed: After the upgrade, the cron job brings the clicks re-clicked before 1.9.79 to one visit each, a little every minute; until it reaches one, the reports count it at each of its visits. Keep the cron job running. A click it cannot bring over is named in p202 system dataengine; after an hour of tries that fail with an error of its own it is skipped, and still counted at each of its visits. A lock, a timeout or a lost connection does not count towards that, however long it lasts

Changed: Between installing the files of a new version and running its upgrade, an API request that fails says the database needs an upgrade and where to run it (a 503), instead of a bare server error; so do the legacy v1 and v2 reports, the Android install intake and the Apple postback endpoints. Files older than the database (rolled back) are not sent to the upgrade: the API answers as before, and the sync worker says to deploy the newer files

Changed: A tracking link or landing page whose p202_consent is anything but 1 (false, off, an empty value) withholds the visitor's signals; before, only 0 did and the rest read as consent. The landing page reads it however the tracker does, p202.consent and p202_consent[] included
Fixed: A site whose name has www. inside it (awww.example.com) is filed as its own domain, not with the name it makes without it (aexample.com). Clicks already filed stay where they are

Changed: The page that connects an AI assistant shows the app's name and site as what the approval link says, and that whoever started the connection gets the access; it no longer calls them verified. Allow a connection only if you started it yourself

Changed: After an upgrade, tracking links look up their ids afresh instead of reading what the previous version cached, so the first clicks after an upgrade each make one more database read; so do the bot-range and browser checks

Changed: When a cron run was recorded in the last five minutes, turning AutoCron on in Settings no longer simply refuses: it says why AutoCron may not be needed and offers to turn it on anyway, since anyone can open the cron address

Fixed: Security. Reading a user's preferences through the API or the CLI showed the account's integration secrets (the ClickBank, JVZoo, Zaxaa and IPQS keys, the Slack webhook, RevContent and the Landing Page Optimizer's keys). It says only whether each one is stored. If anyone who should not see them held an API key, replace those secrets at each network

New: Clicks record Google Ads' iOS click ids (gbraid, wbraid) and TikTok's click id (ttclid) beside the gclid, from direct links and landing pages. They are in the Visitors download, the API and the CLI, and the new [[gbraid]], [[wbraid]] and [[ttclid]] tokens send them on

Fixed: Clicks record Microsoft Advertising's msclkid and Meta's fbclid, so [[msclkid]] and [[fbclid]] fill with the click's ids. No version since at least 1.9.55 kept either, and a click recorded before 1.9.79 has neither, which cannot be recovered. Both are in the Visitors download, the API and the CLI

Fixed: Security. My Account, 3rd Party API Integrations showed the first account's network integrations and their API keys to other users. It shows your own networks, and a saved API key is no longer shown. If other users can open that page on your install, get new API keys from your networks and save them there

Fixed: Security. My Account, 3rd Party API Integrations put your saved IPQualityScore, ClickBank and Zaxaa keys, Slack webhook and JVZoo secret key into the page. It says only that each is saved and, for one of 12 characters or more, its last four characters: leave the field empty to keep it, or paste a new one to replace it. If someone who should not see these secrets could view that page, replace them at each network

Fixed: The CLI's TOTAL row across profiles (report summary, dashboard) computes EPC, CPC, conversion rate, ROI and CPA from the summed figures instead of adding each profile's, and never adds money in different currencies; GET /reports/summary now says which currency its money is in

Changed: New installs, and every account made from 1.9.79 on, start with privacy set to Enabled for European Traffic: visitors from Europe get no tracking cookies and a masked address. Accounts that existed before keep their setting; change it under My Account, Personal Settings

Fixed: Get Links hands out https:// links when you use Prosper202 over HTTPS or save your tracking domain with https://, the same links the API and p202 tracker get-url give; it wrote http:// always. The Postback / Pixel and API integrations pages follow a tracking domain saved with https:// or http:// too

New: Your AI assistant can create, change and delete text ads, and put one on a tracking link. A connection approved before this version that may make changes needs connecting again to change text ads

New: A redirector's whole rule set can be saved in one step through the API (PUT /rotators/{id}/rules), p202 rotator set-rules and the MCP tool rotator_set_rules, as the Redirector page saves it: all of it or nothing, and a dry run shows what would change. The MCP tools also create, update and delete redirectors
Changed: A redirector's rules are tried in the order you set, so a new rule can go ahead of the others; the upgrade keeps each redirector's order as it was

Fixed: Rule values written through the API are stored as the Redirector page stores them ("United States(US), Canada(CA)" no longer misses Canada), and a device written with a capital, which never matches, is refused

Fixed: Security. A user who could open Setup could rename a traffic source of another user and take it into their own account. A traffic source is now renamed only by its own user. Update as soon as you can, then check each user's Setup › Traffic Sources for a source that is missing

Fixed: The PayKickstart integration works now, for vendors: put subid=[[subid]] on your PayKickstart checkout link, paste the IPN URL into each product's IPN Integration tab and save each PayKickstart campaign's IPN secret key, and every sale, rebill and refund is recorded on the click that sent the buyer. PayKickstart's Affiliate IPN cannot update conversions (it does not carry your click), and the page now says so

New: Every conversion says how its click was found: named by the postback, pixel or upload (click id), by a tracking cookie, by a landing page's visitor id, or guessed from the visitor's IP address. Group Overview's new Match method level, p202 conversion match-methods and the API show each campaign's conversions and income by how they were matched

Fixed: Traffic-source postbacks are sent only to public addresses. A Postback URL pixel aimed at this server's own network or a cloud metadata address is refused when it is saved and is not called when a conversion fires it (the outbox marks it failed with the reason); a redirect to such an address is not followed. A receiver on your own network needs P202_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_NETWORKS in 202-config.php

Fixed: The JVZoo integration works now, for affiliates and vendors: put tid=[[subid]] on your JVZoo affiliate link (or subid=[[subid]] on your buy link), paste the page's Affiliate IPN URL (or Vendor JVZIPN URL) into JVZoo and save your JVZIPN secret key, and every sale and rebill is recorded on the click that sent the buyer, and every refund and chargeback takes it back

Fixed: LTV webhooks, the Landing Page Optimizer's among them, are sent: the cron job sends what is due every minute, where nothing a default install ran sent them. After the upgrade, the events of the last 7 days that were waiting are sent, oldest first; older ones are not sent, and the webhook's delivery log shows them as expired

Fixed: ClickBank's Instant Notifications work for every account now: each sale is recorded for the account whose ClickBank secret key decrypts it. They read account 1's key only, and decrypted with a cipher ClickBank does not use, so no notification was read. Add tid=[[subid]] to your HopLink, save your secret key, choose INS version 8.0 and press Test URL

New: Settings shows how old the GeoIP database behind visitor locations is (the one Prosper202 ships is from 2018), and can keep it current: enter your free MaxMind GeoLite account ID and licence key, and the cron job downloads the new database weekly, checks it and swaps it in. A failed download keeps the database you have and says why
Fixed: A GeoIP database that cannot be opened no longer stops a click; the visitor is recorded without a location, and the error log says why

Fixed: LTV webhooks are sent only to public addresses. Azure's 168.63.129.16 and IPv6 spellings of loopback and the cloud metadata address (::ffff:169.254.169.254) were let through and called; such a webhook is now refused when it is saved, and its deliveries are logged "blocked" and not sent. A receiver on your own network needs P202_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_NETWORKS in 202-config.php

Changed: A pixel that names no click guesses it from the visitor's IP address only for an account with Match conversions by IP address on (Personal Settings, under Advanced). New accounts start with it off; accounts from before 1.9.79 keep it on, and choosing Off there stops the guesses. A visitor your privacy setting holds back is never matched by IP address
Fixed: The global and universal pixels guess a click from the IP address among the clicks of the account whose campaign the pixel names, not the first account's

New: A report breakdown from the API or the CLI says when it has more rows than it returned, and the CLI's losers, winners, crosstab and campaign optimize read every page they need instead of the first 50 rows

Fixed: An LTV subscription that stops renewing is marked past due once its period and grace days are over, and canceled 30 days later, by the cron job every hour; nothing a default install ran did it, so it stayed active and counted in MRR. After the upgrade the ones that lapsed meanwhile are moved, oldest first, and one canceled long ago counts in churn only if its cancel date falls in the last 90 days

Fixed: The group report (GET /reports/groups, p202 report groups) answers EPC, CPC, conversion rate, ROI and CPA to the decimals the summary and the breakdown answer them to; it answered them unrounded, so the same traffic showed two figures

Fixed: p202 report breakeven shows the conversion rate and average CPC report breakdown shows for the same traffic; it replaced them with conversions per click and a rounded CPC. The rate break-even uses is its own column, click_conv_rate

Fixed: ClickBank rebills are recorded on the click that sent the buyer, each under its own receipt, and a refund, chargeback or returned eCheck takes the sale back by what ClickBank says you lost. Cancellations record nothing. For a subscription, set the campaign's When a click converts more than once to Add them up

New: A dead LTV webhook can be revived (LTV Settings, PUT /ltv/webhooks/{id}, p202 ltv webhooks revive): it keeps its id, URL and secret, so the Landing Page Optimizer needs no pairing again, and it is sent the events of the last 7 days it did not get, which are held while it is dead

Fixed: Adding or changing one redirector rule through the API or the CLI is refused when the rule would have no criterion, as the Redirector page refuses it: such a rule matches every visitor, so one call sent all of a redirector's traffic to it. Rules already saved that way keep working as before, and the Redirector page lists them as matching any visitor

Fixed: Security. A sync calls its profiles' URLs only at public https:// addresses, with no redirect followed: a profile pointed at this server's own network or a cloud metadata address is refused (two installs on one machine or network need P202_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_NETWORKS in 202-config.php). A sync reads at most 8 MiB of one answer, 200 pages of one list and 900 seconds in all, and a queued job keeps the profiles' API keys encrypted, and none once it ends

New: An admin can list the traffic sources taken into another user's account before this fix, and move each back to the user whose traffic source accounts name it (GET /system/traffic-source-owners, p202 system traffic-source-owners). Nothing moves by itself: a source that may have been shared on purpose moves only to a user you name

New: Offline conversions for Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising (Setup › Offline Conversions): your conversions as Google Ads' (Data Manager or Uploads template) or Microsoft Advertising's import file, with a conversion name per campaign and Google's consent columns. Only conversions whose click was named, not guessed from an IP address, are sent. Download a file, or give the platform a private URL it fetches on a schedule; also GET /conversions/offline-export and p202 conversion offline-export

Fixed: A redirector rule saved as "all" sends every visitor to the rule from a landing page's offer link too, as it did from the redirector link; it sent them to the default. ALL is read the same way in any case and beside other values, by both links, the Redirector page and the Rotator Breakdown, and is accepted on an IP rule, which was refused as not an IP address

Fixed: p202 report losers, winners and crosstab, and the offers p202 campaign optimize ranks, show the cost, CPC, profit and EPC p202 report breakdown shows for the same rows; they rounded them, so a cost or CPC below a cent read 0. With --payout, the profit at your payout is its own column, payout_net, beside the recorded total_net
Fixed: LTV Settings deletes only the webhook, field or integration a row names: an id sent as 12abc deleted number 12, and is refused now

Fixed: p202 campaign optimize shows the conversion rate the reports show (conversions per click-through) and calls its own rate, which its break-even CPC uses, conversions per click; it called that one CVR, so on landing-page traffic it read lower than every report
Fixed: API Integrations says when the Landing Page Optimizer is not receiving events because its webhook is dead or gone, where it said Connected

Fixed: The cron job runs one at a time, however long a run takes: a run over ten minutes had a second one started beside it, and one that died kept every run for the next ten minutes from doing anything. The web server needs to be able to write 202-cronjobs/ (or read a cron-run.lock made there); a run that cannot take its lock says why instead of running without it
Fixed: Webhooks subscribed to subscription.changed hear when the hourly sweep makes a subscription past_due or canceled, for changes in the last 7 days

Fixed: When an API key, or an AI app connected before an update let it do more, is refused for a scope it lacks, the refusal names the scope and what grants it: connecting the AI app again with the access it names, or a new key with that scope. The p202 CLI and the MCP tools pass it on

Fixed: Customers whose company was stored before that company existed are attached by the LTV maintenance job even when an account has more than 2,000 whose company is nothing but spaces; those are stored as having no company, where they held the job back on every run

Changed: The API answers a customer's revenue, refunds and MRR (and its subscriptions', revenue events' and line items' amounts, and its engagement) as numbers, as the LTV summary does, rather than as text such as "54.12500", and its custom_fields as an object even when it holds none
Fixed: Security. The container image no longer ships the test suite, whose helper scripts could act on a database with no sign-in; in a checkout served as the web root they now answer 404

Fixed: Changing one redirector rule's destinations through the API or the CLI (PUT /rotators/{id}/rules/{ruleId}, p202 rotator rule-update) keeps each destination sent with its id, as saving the whole rule set does; every destination took a new id, so the clicks it had sent were listed under no redirect in Group Overview

Fixed: Customer LTV's Companies, Products and customer pages act only on the record a button or the merge dialog names: an id sent as 12abc merged, deleted, erased or unlinked number 12, and is refused now

Fixed: Android installs waiting for their click are settled in turns. Installs that could not be settled (their install token no longer verified, or their stored install no longer read) took every place in the cron job's batch, so no other app's installs were settled. A failed settle is now retried less and less often, one that can never be read is settled as a bad token 24 hours after it arrived, and Analyze › Mobile Apps says how many are failing

Fixed: p202 campaign optimize said there was no salvage offer when it could not read the other campaigns' figures (a server error, a key without the scope, an unreachable server); it now fails with the error and what to do next. Its ranked campaigns carry their ids, and its next step names the salvage campaign's id where it printed a placeholder, and names none when no other campaign earns more per click
Fixed: A customer the LTV maintenance job attaches to its company shows that change as its last update (updated_at); it kept the time of its last other change

Fixed: The container image installs the Composer dependencies in composer.lock, the versions the release zip ships, instead of whatever matched composer.json the day it was built; a build stops when the lock is out of date with composer.json

Changed: The rest of the API's LTV reads answer money, averages and rates as numbers and counts and times as whole numbers too: subscriptions, the LTV breakdowns by campaign, traffic source account, landing page and product, products, companies and the ABM views. They answered text such as "29.99000" and "4", so a subscription's amount was a number in a customer's detail and text in the subscription list

Fixed: Installing again into a database of the same name no longer replays the previous install's API answers: a create sent with an Idempotency-Key the old install had answered was answered as done and nothing was created, and the old install's proposed changes were listed and could be applied. The API's server-side state is now kept per install; the server log names the old directory, which is left as it was, to remove

Fixed: Multi-touch attribution stopped for the whole install when one identity merge (two visitors found to be one person) could not be re-queued: that merge failed first on every run of the attribution worker and nothing after it ran. A failing merge is now recorded and tried again later, the rest of the run carries on, and the Attribution page says how many merges are failing. A merge whose own data cannot be re-queued is set aside with the reason; attribution-worker.php --retry-now tries it again

Fixed: Product analytics are delivered one run at a time: 202-cronjobs/sync-messaging.php ran beside a delivery still going after ten minutes and beside the cron job's hourly one, sending each waiting event twice, and one that died kept the next ten minutes of runs from delivering. An install whose web server cannot write 202-cronjobs/ needs an empty analytics-delivery.lock there, as for cron-run.lock

Fixed: The same with P202_SERVER_STATE_DIR set (the Coolify stack's api_state volume): each install keeps its API state in a directory of its own inside it, so a database installed again starts with none of the old one's. What an earlier version kept at the top of the directory is left there, and the server log says what to copy or remove. After restoring the database from a backup, still empty the install's directory before the first API request

New: Settings tells an admin when a traffic source is in another user's account, lists each one with whose accounts name it, and moves it back after a confirmation that says what will move. The same list and move as the API and the CLI, for owners who use neither

Fixed: The answer to a PayKickstart, JVZoo or ClickBank notification naming a click the account does not have now names that platform's own field and the link variable that fills it (custom_subid, JVZoo's tid or the buy link's subid, ClickBank's tracking code or extclid), as the answer to one naming no click does, and one rule words both for every platform

Fixed: p202 diff stops on a profile URL the server will not call, as p202 sync does, with the same hint naming the profile to repoint and P202_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_NETWORKS. It diffed from your machine instead, making the calls the server had refused and never showing why

New: A traffic source that more than one user's traffic source accounts name, which moving it back never cleared, can be split from Settings (or the API and CLI): it stays where it is and each other user gets a copy of their own, which their accounts then name
Fixed: Security. A user switched off or removed in My Account, Users stayed signed in on every browser that already was. Their next request now signs them out, and nothing it asked for is done

Fixed: Security. Signing out left the browser's remember-me key valid, so a copy of its cookie still signed in for up to 14 days, and switching a user off left all of theirs valid, so a remembered browser signed back in once the user was switched on again. Signing out now deletes that browser's key (the user's other remembered browsers stay signed in), and switching a user off in My Account, Users or through the API deletes every one of theirs

Fixed: A sync writes a redirector's rules on the other install whole or not at all. When the other install refused one (since this version, a rule with no criterion), its redirector was left with its own rules removed and only the synced rules before the refused one
Fixed: The first page opened with only a remember-me cookie (Keep me signed in) ran without the user's roles, so a page such as My Account, Users sent the user away. It has them now
Fixed: Setup › Traffic Sources refuses an account edit whose link names the account with more than its id (12abc), where it saved the change to account 12

Fixed: p202 report losers and winners with --aff-campaign-id priced every click at a payout of 0 when they could not read the campaign's payout (a server error, a refused key, an unreachable server); they now fail with the error and what to do next. An answer with no payout in it is an error in every command that reads one, and a campaign whose payout is 0 is still priced at 0

Fixed: The Redirector page no longer drops every destination but the first of a rule made through the API with several destinations and Split test off when you save; it shows the rule as the split test the redirect links make of it, with each destination's weight

Fixed: Security. Changing a password left every browser kept signed in able to sign in again by its cookie, a stolen copy included. A new password (Personal settings, the reset link, My Account, Users, or the API) now ends them all; the browser making the change on Personal settings stays signed in. A browser already signed in is signed out too

Fixed: Security. Changing or resetting a password now signs out every other browser signed in as the user, not only those kept signed in; the browser making the change on Personal settings stays signed in. Switching a user off ends their sessions for good, also one that was idle meanwhile

Fixed: A sync (p202 sync, POST /sync/jobs) keeps a redirector rule that is switched off as switched off on the target. A rule an older install stored with no status, which the redirects skip, reached the target as an active rule and started taking that redirector's traffic there

Fixed: Slack notices are sent only to public https:// addresses and give up after 2 seconds. API Integrations and the API now refuse the same webhook URLs (plain http, this server's own network, a cloud metadata address); a notice that is not sent is logged with why, and no longer holds the request that sent it, which made ClickBank's test fail on servers without PHP-FPM. A receiver on your own network needs P202_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_NETWORKS in 202-config.php. If you saved an http:// or internal webhook before, Slack notices stop until you save it again as the https://hooks.slack.com/... URL Slack shows

New: Connect an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT and other apps that use MCP) to your Prosper202. It reads your reports and campaigns and, only if you allow it, proposes or makes changes. You approve each connection on your own install, and remove it under My Account, Personal Settings, API keys. Needs Prosper202 ClickServer Pro

New: p202 mcp lets AI apps on your computer (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor) work with Prosper202 through the Go CLI: read only if you choose, or with every change made a proposal you apply yourself
Changed: A tracking link that cannot reach the database answers 503 (try again later) where it has nowhere saved to send the visitor, instead of a broken page
Changed: Two Prosper202 installs that share one memcache server no longer read each other's cached entries
Changed: The sign-in log shows whether each attempt passed, failed or did not complete (also GET /system/login-log and p202 system login-log)
Changed: Get Links refuses a cloaking setting other than the three it offers

Changed: The Docker image is built on PHP 8.3.36, which fixes two critical PHP security vulnerabilities. If you run Prosper202 in Docker, rebuild the image (on Coolify, redeploy; with docker compose, docker compose build --pull and docker compose up -d) and check that php -v in the web container says 8.3.36

Fixed: Security. This release fixes security problems on tracking links, landing pages, redirectors and the account pages. Update as soon as you can, then check My Account, User Management for users you do not recognise

Fixed: A new install stopped on step 2, "Get your license key", with a server error, so the key had to be entered by hand. The page now opens on a new install, before Prosper202 has created its database tables. On an install that is already set up, a license key sent back to that page is no longer repeated in the address of the sign-in page it moves you on to

Fixed: When the database refused a change or a read failed, several pages said the change was saved, showed an empty value (a cron job that never ran, no DNI networks, no ClickServer key) or stopped on a PHP error. They now say the save failed or show the database error page, and the error is recorded

Fixed: Direct links filled the offer URL's tokens ([[c1]] to [[c4]], [[t202kw]], [[gclid]], the UTM tokens and others) with nothing, and [[cpc]], [[payout]] and [[cpa]] wrongly. They carry the click's values again
Fixed: A redirector rule that sends visitors to a campaign with URL rotation always sent its first URL

Fixed: Keywords, place and ISP names, referring sites and device models longer than their columns were stored cut and stored again on every click, and an IPv6 visitor could be shown under another visitor's address
Fixed: Keywords, c1 to c4 and gclid values holding a quote or a backslash were stored with extra backslashes
Fixed: A redirector re-click lost the click's customer, text ad and first values
Fixed: A sign-in the database could not record ended on a blank page, and a right password could be logged as a failed sign-in
Fixed: The legacy reports API (v1 and v2) answered 500 for several reports and filters, and ignored a c1 to c4 filter of 0

Fixed: The Customer API key on Personal Settings is checked with Tracking202 before it is saved, and the page says the key could not be checked, rather than not valid, when Tracking202 does not answer

Fixed: The cron job reports its own database failures, and an hourly or daily job that fails part way is tried again at the next run instead of the next day. A brief database error no longer sends every signed-in page to the upgrade page

Fixed: Bulk upsert (API and CLI) says which rows were stored when the database rolls a batch back, marks the rows to send again, and a retry under the same Idempotency-Key no longer stores a batch twice

Fixed: Turning AutoCron on in Settings was refused on every install because opening a page counted as your cron job. It works now, and when the AutoCron service refuses a local or private address, Settings says to use a cron job
Fixed: A 202-config.php from an older install, without the read-only connection, no longer stops pages, Spy and the API with a PHP error
Fixed: p202 conversion simulate reads the click id from the field your offer URL puts [[subid]] in, and refuses instead of guessing when it cannot tell
Fixed: On a new install running MariaDB, clicks that arrived at the same moment could go unrecorded. They are all recorded now

Important: This upgrade changes your database in place (a new setting for the scheduled click deletion, and the in-app chat's two message tables are removed). Back up the Prosper202 database before you start: restoring that backup is the only way back

New: The web UI's pages can be done from the REST API and the p202 CLI: Update CPC, subids and revenue uploads; Setup's landing-page code, pixels, postback URLs and traffic-source variables; Account settings and integrations; the Analyze pages' dimensions and filters, Visitors, Spy (p202 click list --follow) and the Group Overview; and every LTV write. documentation/cli/12-ui-parity.md maps each page to its route and command, and says what is still partial

Changed: Chat with the Tracking202 team is a new chat box that connects straight to the chat service: replies arrive as they are sent, you can see when the team has read your message and when someone is typing, and announcements are listed beside your conversation. Prosper202 no longer stores or relays chat messages; it only fetches a pass for the chat box. The box stays hidden on an install with no customer API key. Product analytics (Prosper202Messenger('update' and 'trackEvent')) work as before

Changed: The chat box's pass request also tells the portal which Prosper202 version this install runs, so we can see which versions are in use and who still needs an update. It is sent only with the request the chat box already makes (an install with no customer API key sends nothing), and nothing new reaches the browser

Changed: The Go CLI (p202) needs a Prosper202 ClickServer Pro subscription or trial. Without one its commands stop with a message linking the trial (error category licence, exit code 6). The web app, the PHP CLI (bin/p202) and direct API calls keep working with the same API key, and if my.tracking202.com cannot be reached the CLI keeps working

Changed: The REST API refuses what it cannot do, with a 422 or 404 naming the field, where it used to answer success having done less: an unknown or misspelt field, a number, date or switch it cannot read, an id in the path that is not one, and ?dry_run=1 on a write that has no preview. Check scripts that relied on a field being ignored
Changed: API answers give money and counts as JSON numbers, and report periods (today, last 7 days and the rest) are the account's calendar days, as on the report pages

Changed: An API key is held to its user's role, as the pages hold that user: Setup, Update, goals and personal settings need the page's permission, a deactivated user's keys stop working, and an Admin can no longer make itself Super user

Fixed: Security. Visitors, Spy and the click breakdown listed every account's visitors, the Overview chart and the daily email counted every account's clicks, and a record naming another account's record by id showed that account's names, payouts and settings. Each now reads the signed-in account's own records

Fixed: Security. The password reset email's link was built from the request's host, so a stranger could have it point elsewhere; it uses your stored tracking domain. A blanked session token no longer passes the forms' token check

Fixed: The privacy setting does what it says: "Enabled for European Traffic" works, every stored visitor address is masked under privacy (the full address was kept on clicks, conversions and app installs), and the setting of the account that owns the link applies, not only the install's

Fixed: Reports count days and hours in your account's time zone, through daylight-saving changes and half-hour offsets, and follow a change of zone without signing in again. A renamed zone your account uses (Europe/Kiev) is no longer lost when Personal Settings is saved

Fixed: Automatic click-data deletion deleted almost nothing, and "Delete click data from before" could delete a click from the day itself. Both now delete exactly the clicks older than the day you set, from every click table, and the reports are recomputed from the clicks that remain

Fixed: Tracking links. Click cookies work on an install served from a non-default port, Get Links' landing-page links record their clicks, links on an install with no tracking domain name the address you use, and cloaked redirects work behind a TLS proxy or in a subdirectory
Fixed: Redirectors. An offer rotator's rules choose by weight, an IP rule matches an address however it is written, and the Rotator Breakdown counts each rule's own clicks

Fixed: Upload Revenue Reports picks the commission column, not an order total or a sale id; a decimal comma (12,50) is skipped instead of read as 1250; a very long line is read as one; and a large report lists its first 1,000 skipped lines and counts the rest by reason
Fixed: An hour whose report rollup failed is retried instead of being marked done, and report rows follow a traffic source account or campaign that moves

New: Go CLI for people and AI agents: p202 commands --brief lists every command with the UI page it does, p202 search finds a command by a page's name or the task's words, and a command no longer exits 0 for something it did not do

Important: This upgrade changes your database in place and cannot be undone. Back up the Prosper202 database (a full mysqldump, or your host's snapshot) before you start: restoring that backup is the only way back

New: Android app install tracking. Register an app from its Google Play link and send campaign clicks to the store link Prosper202 builds; the Prosper202 Android SDK reports each install, and the events after it, as a conversion on the click that sent the user to the store

New: Android fraud signals and limits: Play Integrity checks (off, observe or require, per app), click-to-install time flags for click injection and click spamming, goals reached implausibly fast, and per-app install and per-install event caps

New: SKAdNetwork and AdAttributionKit measurement for iOS apps: receive Apple's signed postbacks, verify their signatures, and report installs, re-engagements and decoded revenue by app, ad network, source and country. Conversion values are configured on the server, so changing them needs no App Store resubmission
New: Android SDK (Kotlin), and an iOS SDK that evaluates your goals on the device and sets the matching conversion value
New: Mobile Apps pages under Setup and Analyze: register apps from a store link, build the store link a campaign should use, edit each app's goals, and report both platforms side by side

New: Goals. Define what counts as a conversion (an install, an event with conditions, the Nth purchase, a running total, a step after another goal, within a time window) and what it is worth. Goals are versioned, shared by web campaigns and apps, and each campaign can pay for each goal at its own payout

New: Web events. Add event= to your postbacks and pixels, call POST /api/v3/events, or use p202.track() on a landing page to record what a visitor does after the click; the campaign's goals decide what each event is worth, and on a campaign without goals event= is an ordinary conversion

New: Conversion ledger. Every amount on a click is its own row recording what produced it, and a click's value can be explained row by row in Visitors, Spy, the API and the CLI. A campaign setting chooses whether repeat conversions keep the latest payout (the default) or add up
New: Correction URLs on traffic source postbacks, so a network that already heard about a conversion is told when it is corrected or reversed

Changed: Multi-touch attribution is rebuilt. Journeys join a visitor's own clicks using first-party signals only (never IP addresses), under last-touch, first-touch, linear, time-decay and position-based models, with a new Attribution dashboard and scheduled CSV exports to signed webhooks

Changed: The whole app, including sign-in, the installer and the upgrader, uses one Bootstrap 5.3 interface with light and dark themes. The separate 202-Mobile pages are retired in favour of the responsive pages

Changed: Traffic source postbacks from the global postback and the universal pixel are queued with the conversion and sent from a retrying outbox, so a failed send is retried instead of lost, and deleting a conversion cancels or retracts the postbacks queued for it
Changed: Without a transaction id, the global postback and the universal pixel convert a click once, as the global pixel does. Send a transaction id to record several conversions on one click

Fixed: Security. The setup wizard could rewrite the configuration of an installed instance; the upgrade and license-key pages accepted a post without the session token; the Get Links and redirector pages accepted another account's campaign, traffic source and rule ids; and the ClickServer switch did not check its permission. Each is now refused
Fixed: Deleting a user revokes their API keys, which used to keep working, and removes their data in the same step
Fixed: Password reset works again; report pages no longer pick up filters set in another browser tab; and filter menus list only your own account's values

Fixed: Upgrading from 1.9.55 keeps transaction ids that differ only in letter case, runs one upgrade at a time, keeps going if the browser times out on a large database, and leaves exactly the schema a fresh install creates
